tiered_hints.tier_1_conceptual: Consider how many total nearest-neighbor bonds exist on a square lattice with periodic boundaries where each site has four nearest neighbors, and account for the energy contributed by each parallel bond.
tiered_hints.tier_2_structural: Structural Setup (Ising Hamiltonian, Z_2 Symmetry, Lattice-Gas & Binary-Alloy Mappings): On a square lattice with periodic boundary conditions, each site has coordination number $z = 4$.
tiered_hints.tier_3_worked_step: Because each bond connects 2 sites, the total number of distinct nearest-neighbor pairs is $N_{\text{bonds}} = \frac{1}{2} z N = \frac{1}{2}(4)(250) = 500$. In the fully aligned ground state, $s_i s_j = (+1)(+1) = +1$ for every bond. The total energy is $E_{\text{ground}} = -J N_{\text{bonds}} = -2.4\text{ meV} \times 500 = -1200.0\text{ meV}$.

tiered_hints.tier_1_conceptual: Identify how many nearest-neighbor bonds have their relative spin alignment altered by flipping one interior spin, and evaluate the difference in bond energy between an antiparallel pair and a parallel pair.
tiered_hints.tier_2_structural: Structural Setup (Ising Hamiltonian, Z_2 Symmetry, Lattice-Gas & Binary-Alloy Mappings): Flipping a single site $k$ affects exactly its $z = 4$ nearest-neighbor bonds.
tiered_hints.tier_3_worked_step: Before the flip, each bond contributed $-J$ to the energy; after the flip, each bond has antiparallel spins and contributes $+J$. The change per bond is $+J - (-J) = +2J$. For $z = 4$ bonds, the net energy change is $\Delta E = 2 z J = 2(4)(2.4\text{ meV}) = 19.2\text{ meV}$.

tiered_hints.tier_1_conceptual: Compare how the energetic cost of an enclosing domain boundary scales with its geometric perimeter/area versus how the number of possible boundary configurations (entropy) scales in one dimension versus two dimensions.
tiered_hints.tier_2_structural: Structural Setup (1D Kramers-Wannier Transfer Matrix & Absence of 1D Phase Transitions): In 1D, a domain wall is a zero-dimensional point separating two semi-infinite domains.
tiered_hints.tier_3_worked_step: Its energy cost is constant ($\Delta E = 2J$), but its entropy $\Delta S = k_B \ln N$ diverges as $N \to \infty$, meaning $\Delta F = 2J - k_B T \ln N < 0$ for any $T > 0$. In 2D, an island of reversed spins is enclosed by a 1D contour of perimeter $P$. The energy cost grows linearly with perimeter ($\Delta E = 2 J P$), while the number of self-avoiding closed contours of perimeter $P$ scales as $\mu^P$. The free energy change is $\Delta F \ge (2J - k_B T \ln \mu) P$. For $T < T_c \approx 2J / (k_B \ln \mu)$, $\Delta F > 0$ and increases with perimeter, suppressing large domain fluctuations and stabilizing spontaneous order.
